21 The Court also has supplemental jurisdiction over CVS’s related state-law claims pursuant to 28

10                                    The Parties’ Business Relationship

11                     10.   On or about October 25, 2018, CVS and Swyft entered into a written Master

12 Rental and Services Agreement (the “Master Agreement”) pursuant to which Defendants agreed to
13 provide and operate automated retail machine kiosks for the sale of CVS-branded products. A true
14 and correct copy of the Master Agreement is attached hereto as Exhibit “A” and is incorporated
15 herein by this reference.
16                     11.   As part of the parties’ relationship and under the Master Agreement, CVS

17 developed and supplied wrap designs for Swyft’s kiosks which were distinctive to CVS, including
18 color schemes, graphics, and iconography specific to CVS (the “Wrap Artwork”). CVS furnished
19 those designs to Swyft solely for use on kiosks operated under the parties’ business relationship.
20                     12.    Section 18(d) of the Master Agreement provides that materials furnished by

21 CVS, including designs and related materials, remain the property of CVS and must be returned
22 promptly upon request.
23                                           Settlement Agreement

24                     13.   A dispute arose between the parties relating to their respective rights and

25 obligations pursuant to the Master Agreement which ultimately resulted in the parties entering into
26 a Settlement Agreement and Limited Release of Claims (the “Settlement Agreement”) on or about
27 October 17, 2022. A true and correct copy of the Settlement Agreement is attached hereto as
28 Exhibit “B” and is incorporated herein by this reference.

 1                     14.   Pursuant to the terms of the Settlement Agreement, Swyft agreed to pay

 2 CVS a total of $1,800,000.00 (the “Settlement Amount”) pursuant to a payment schedule outlined
 3 in Section 1 of the Settlement Agreement.
 4                     15.   In particular, Swyft agreed to pay CVS $600,000.00 within seven (7) days

 5 of Swyft’s anticipated closing of its Series A-2 financing round.
 6                     16.   The Settlement Agreement further provides that, so long as Swyft paid the

 7 initial $600,000.00 installment by January 4, 2023, Swyft would be required to pay the remaining
 8 $1,200,000.00 of the Settlement Amount in equal monthly installments of $33,333 through March
 9 5, 2024, with any remaining unpaid balance due and payable in full no later than April 5, 2024.
10                     17.   The Settlement Agreement further provides, in Section 2, that if any

11 Settlement Payment is not paid on or before the date due, the full remaining unpaid balance of the
12 Settlement Amount shall immediately accelerate and become due and payable to CVS within five
13 (5) days of such default, together with daily compound interest at the rate of 0.05% on the full
14 amount owing until paid. The Settlement Agreement also provides that CVS is not required to
15 provide notice of default for these terms to take effect.
16                               Swyft’s Breach of the Settlement Agreement

17                     18.   Swyft paid the initial $600,000 installment timely and thereafter made

18 monthly payments of approximately $33,333 for a certain period of time.
19                     19.   Pursuant to Section 1 of the Settlement Agreement, Swyft was required to

20 pay the remaining unpaid balance of the Settlement Amount in full as a final “balloon payment”
21 no later than April 5, 2024. Swyft failed to make that balloon payment when due.
22                     20.   Swyft’s failure to make the balloon payment on or before April 5, 2024

23 constituted a material breach and event of default under the Settlement Agreement, triggering the
24 acceleration provisions in Section 2.
25                     21.   Swyft continued to make the monthly payments of $33,000 for a period of

26 time thereafter. CVS at no time agreed to modify the Settlement Agreement or to waive Swyft’s
27 default or CVS’s contractual right to demand immediate payment of the full accelerated balance.
28

 1                     22.   On or about May 2025, Swyft ceased making any further payments

 2 altogether to CVS pursuant to the Settlement Agreement. Swyft has failed and refused, and
 3 continues to fail and refuse, to pay the accelerated balance owing despite its clear contractual
 4 obligation to do so.
 5                     23.   Since Swyft made the $600,000 initial payment, and approximately 28

 6 monthly installment payments of about $33,000 each from early 2023 until around May 2025,
 7 totaling approximately $924,000, this left an unpaid principal balance outstanding and owing to
 8 CVS pursuant to the Settlement Agreement in an amount no less than $276,000.
 9                     24.   As a result of Swyft’s defaults and the resulting acceleration of the

10 remaining balance of the Settlement Amount, $276,000 in unpaid principal is now immediately
11 due and owing by Swyft to CVS, exclusive of accrued interest at the contractually agreed rate.
12                     25.   Between at least July and December 2025, through its counsel and various

13 executives by email and other communications, CVS repeatedly demanded that Swyft pay the
14 overdue, outstanding balance of the Settlement Amount. Swyft, however, failed to substantively
15 respond to these demands and/or cure its default under the Settlement Agreement.
16                                         CVS’s Resulting Damages

17                     26.   Despite CVS’s numerous reminders to Swyft that it was in breach of its

18 payment obligations pursuant to the Settlement Agreement, Swyft continues to fail and refuse to
19 cure its outstanding breaches of the Settlement Agreement or to pay CVS the balance of the
20 Settlement Amount now past due and owing. CVS is further informed and believes, and based
21 thereon alleges, that Swyft has no intention of complying with its remaining obligations pursuant
22 to the Settlement Agreement unless and until ordered to do so.
23                     27.   CVS has performed and fulfilled all its duties and obligations under the

24 terms of the Settlement Agreement and at all relevant times herein, Swyft knew that CVS had
25 performed and fulfilled all of those duties and obligations.
26                     28.   Swyft, on the other hand, has materially breached the Settlement Agreement

27 by failing and refusing to pay CVS the remaining balance due and owing pursuant to the

 1 Settlement Agreement in the amount of no less than $276,000, plus contractually agreed interest,
 2 costs, and related relief.
 3                     29.   As a direct and proximate result of Swyft’s material breaches of the

 4 Settlement Agreement, CVS has suffered, and continues to suffer, damage, harm and loss, as well
 5 as pre-judgment interest thereon, in an amount to be established at trial.
 6                           Swyft’s Unauthorized Use of CVS Kiosk Wrap Design

 7                     30.   Swyft’s authority to use the Wrap Artwork was limited. Swyft was not

 8 authorized to use the Wrap Artwork except in connection with kiosks operated for CVS pursuant
 9 to the parties’ relationship, and CVS did not authorize Swyft to continue using the Wrap Artwork
10 on kiosks operating outside that relationship or in locations not approved by CVS.
11                     31.   On or about March 28, 2025, CVS sent Swyft written correspondence that

12 the wrap design was CVS’s design, that Swyft’s continued use of that design was not authorized,
13 and that CVS demanded that Swyft cease using the wraps. CVS further confirmed in that
14 communication that the parties’ remaining kiosk arrangements would terminate effective July 1,
15 2025.
16                     32.   Thereafter, solely in connection with offboarding discussions, CVS

17 temporarily agreed, solely to avoid the cost and disruption of immediate removal, that certain
18 existing kiosks could retain CVS wraps while decommissioning was underway. CVS expressly
19 prohibited Swyft from moving any kiosk bearing Wrap Artwork to any new or higher-visibility
20 locations, or using Wrap Artwork on any new kiosks or in any new locations.
21                     33.   Notwithstanding CVS’s express limitations and the termination of the

22 parties’ relationship, and since the full decommissioning has been effected, Swyft has continued to
23 display Wrap Artwork on kiosks that were moved or placed in new and high-traffic venues
24 without CVS’s authorization, including numerous airport locations, among others.
25                     34.   CVS has received reports and photographic evidence of such kiosks bearing

26 the Wrap Artwork in the marketplace, causing confusion among CVS employees and members of
27 the public as to whether Swyft’s kiosks remain affiliated with or approved by CVS.

                                             MASTER RENTAL AND SERVICES AGREEMENT
             This Master Rental and Services Agreement {"Agreement") is made as of October 25'\ 2018, {the "Effective Date")
             by and between Swyft Capital, a Delaware corporation having its principal place of business at I40 Geary St, Floor
             7, San Francisco CA 94108 ("Swyft") and CVS Pharmacy, Inc., a Rhode Island corporation, on its own behalf and
             on behalf of its subsidiaries and affiliates, including without limitation Caremark Rx, L.L.C., with an office located
             at One CVS Drive, Woonsocket, Rl 02895 ("Brand Partner").

                                                                BACKGROUND

                      WHEREAS, Brand Partner is in the business of manufacturing and/or retailing of consumer goods;

                      WHEREAS, Swyft is in the business of, among other things, (I) developing and maintaining software and
             hardware systems for automated retail, (2) retailing products through automated retail machines, (3) managing
             Services for the operation of automated retail machines, including maintaining networks of automated retail
             locations, property leases, handling of inventory, warehousing and logistics, and software and hardware
             management, among other things, whether provided by Swyft or by its third-party vendors;

                    WHEREAS, the Parties desire to memorialize the terms and conditions under which Swyft would rent to
            Brand Partner such automated retail machines and related managed Services which may include Services purchased
            by Swyft through its third-party vendors and where Swyft may further develop and operate certain retail channels
            through which Swyft may sell Products obtained from vendors pursuant to the terms outlined in Section 15 Product
            Supply Chain, Replenishment and Right to sell as well as Exhibit C Product Recalls and Returns.



                     NOW, THEREFORE, the parties, in consideration of the covenants contained herein, and other good and
            valuable consideration, the sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, agree as follows:

                                                                 AGREEMENT

                 I.   Purchase of SwyftStores: Services

                          a.   Relationship. Brand Partner acknowledges that, except to the extent the parties may agree
                               otherwise in a written, executed amendment to this Agreement: (i) automated retail machines to be
                               provided hereunder ("SwyftStores"), including hardware components and software components
                               thereof (respectively, "Hardware" and "Software"), will be provided by Swyft and (ii) all
